criteria.support_condition: Comparable enterprise procurement and actual-use data show a substantial gap, and credible causal evidence identifies inadequate business returns as an important explanation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows substantial sustained use and material business returns across enterprises, or credible causal evidence rejects inadequate returns as the asserted explanation.

evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
evidence.explanation: The representative US survey reports work use by 28.1% of employed respondents and daily work use by 10.6%. This challenges a broad absence-of-use reading, but does not isolate enterprise-procured products or establish their returns.

Enterprise leaders reported commercial gains from deployed applications, providing material counterevidence to the proposed lack of benefits. These vendor-sponsored self-reports do not establish net returns or causally explain employee adoption.

evidence.explanation: The survey reports limited conversion of experiments into production and difficulties measuring value. It also identifies data, governance and regulatory barriers, so a purchasing-to-use gap would not by itself establish Zitron's explanation.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Matched enterprise purchasing and usage records, together with credible estimates of net returns and evidence distinguishing inadequate benefits from training, data, governance and integration barriers.
